import pandas as pd


def churn_by_region(df):
    unique = df.drop_duplicates(subset="customer_id", keep="first").copy()
    unique["region"] = unique["region"].fillna("unknown")
    summary = (
        unique.groupby("region", dropna=False)
        .agg(customers=("customer_id", "size"), churned=("churned", "sum"))
        .reset_index()
    )
    summary["churn_rate"] = (summary["churned"] / summary["customers"]).round(4)
    summary = summary.sort_values(["churn_rate", "region"], ascending=[False, True])
    summary = summary.reset_index(drop=True)
    return summary[["region", "customers", "churned", "churn_rate"]]

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):
    rates = df.groupby("mode")["late"].sum().sort_index()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), rates.values.tolist())
    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")
    ax.set_xlabel("Transport mode")
    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")
    return fig

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

variants.code:
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):
    rates = df.groupby("mode", sort=False)["late"].mean()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), rates.values.tolist())
    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")
    ax.set_xlabel("Transport mode")
    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")
    return fig

mistake.title: Modes in the order they happened to appear
mistake.explanation: Rule 2 sorts the modes alphabetically. groupby(sort=False) keeps first-appearance order, which changes between datasets.

variants.code:
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):
    rates = df.groupby("mode")["late"].mean().sort_index()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), rates.values.tolist())
    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), [1 - value for value in rates.values.tolist()], bottom=rates.values.tolist())
    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")
    ax.set_xlabel("Transport mode")
    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")
    return fig

mistake.title: Two stacked series
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for one series. Adding a second bar layer, even as a stacked filler, makes the chart harder to read and fails the review check.

mistake.title: The chart has no title
mistake.explanation: Rule 4 asks for a title. A reader who opens the chart on its own needs to know what it shows.

mistake.title: The y-axis label does not say rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 6 asks for the y-axis label to mention "rate". "Shipments" names the thing being counted, not the number the bars show.

payload.reference:
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):
    rates = df.groupby("mode")["late"].mean().sort_index()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), rates.values.tolist())
    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")
    ax.set_xlabel("Transport mode")
    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")
    return fig

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

mistake.title: Horizontal bars instead of vertical
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for vertical bars. barh() draws them sideways, which the review template does not accept.

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

mistake.title: Modes in the order they happened to appear

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):

    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), rates.values.tolist())
    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")
    ax.set_xlabel("Category")
    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")
    return fig

mistake.title: Horizontal bars instead of vertical
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for vertical bars. barh() draws them sideways, which the review template does not accept.

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

variants.code:
import matplotlib

def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):
    rates = df.groupby("mode")["late"].sum().sort_index()

    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")

    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

mistake.title: Modes in the order they happened to appear
mistake.explanation: Rule 2 sorts the modes alphabetically. groupby(sort=False) keeps first-appearance order, which changes between datasets.

mistake.title: Horizontal bars instead of vertical
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for vertical bars. barh() draws them sideways, which the review template does not accept.

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

mistake.title: Modes in the order they happened to appear
mistake.explanation: Rule 2 sorts the modes alphabetically. groupby(sort=False) keeps first-appearance order, which changes between datasets.

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")

mistake.title: Horizontal bars instead of vertical
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for vertical bars. barh() draws them sideways, which the review template does not accept.

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

    rates = df.groupby("mode")["late"].sum().sort_index()

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

mistake.title: Horizontal bars instead of vertical
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for vertical bars. barh() draws them sideways, which the review template does not accept.

    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

variants.code:
import matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_late_rate_by_mode(df):
    rates = df.groupby("mode")["late"].sum().sort_index()

    ax.bar(rates.index.tolist(), rates.values.tolist())
    ax.set_title("Late delivery rate by transport mode")
    ax.set_xlabel("Transport mode")
    ax.set_ylabel("Late delivery rate")

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

mistake.title: Modes in the order they happened to appear
mistake.explanation: Rule 2 sorts the modes alphabetically. groupby(sort=False) keeps first-appearance order, which changes between datasets.

mistake.title: Horizontal bars instead of vertical
mistake.explanation: Rule 1 asks for vertical bars. barh() draws them sideways, which the review template does not accept.

mistake.title: A line chart for categories
mistake.explanation: Categories such as transport modes have no order between them, so bars fit. A line implies a trend across modes.

mistake.title: Counted late shipments instead of the rate
mistake.explanation: Rule 3 asks for the share of shipments that were late. sum() gives a count, which depends on how many shipments each mode carried.

mistake.explanation: Rule 2 sorts the modes alphabetically. groupby(sort=False) keeps first-appearance order, which changes between datasets.
